accepted.evidence: Turner9758 explicitly distinguishes the l-extension, with Marathi/Konkani māsḷī fish and Prakrit maścalī, from the bare matsya and matsiya branches. Davar masle retains that l-extension; the source final e and nonretroflex l are preserved. The existing promoted extension node is9758-3. No immediate recent donor is established; existing source lect mapping and readings are retained.

Turner5566 section1 explicitly gives Hindi/Marathi ḍoī head. Loss of medial k identifies this branch; do not conflate it with the retained-k head series. No immediate recent donor is established; existing source lect mapping and readings are retained.

Turner5566 section2 gives Gujarati ḍokũ head and Marathi ḍokẽ under *ḍōkka. The survey retained k selects this subsection, unlike Davar ḍoi in section1. No immediate recent donor is established; existing source lect mapping and readings are retained.

Turner6852 explicitly gives Marathi dhūr smoke/haze and Konkani dhuvōru smoke under *dhūmara. The survey r-final smoke word fits this extended family, not bare dhūma6849. Its o vowel is retained. No immediate recent donor is established; existing source lect mapping and readings are retained.

Turner6250 includes the specific beard development through Pali dāṭhikā/Prakrit dāḍhiā, with Hindi dāṛhī/ḍāṛhī and Marathi/Gujarati dāḍhī. Retain both survey initials; the article discusses uncertainty in the older fang–tusk–beard history and possible non-Indo-Aryan influence, which this family assignment does not settle. No immediate recent donor is established; existing source lect mapping and readings are retained.
